segments.voice: Yesterday, Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu made even liberation look light, because love draws Krishna close. But if the love is the point, why practice at all?

Two regulars at the same gym in January. One has a schedule taped to the fridge and shows up whether it's raining or not. The other just loves to run and goes when the wanting pulls. Ask either one, and the other is doing it wrong. Rupa takes up that argument about devotion. And before he lets either side speak, he answers yesterday's question. Practice doesn't build the love. The love is already there. Practice brings it into view.
screen: `THE SCHEDULE ON THE FRIDGE.` → `THE ONE WHO JUST LOVES TO RUN.` → `THE LOVE IS ALREADY THERE.`

segments.voice: Rupa calls it sadhana bhakti, devotion as practice. In paraphrase: it's done with the senses, and by it bhava, the deeper love, is reached. Then the surprising clause. Bhava is eternally real. What practice achieves is its showing up in the heart. A window cleared, not a light manufactured. Then he splits practice in two, and lets each side make its case. The first is vaidhi, practice by rule, done because scripture asks for it. Its best case: the rule is there on the gray mornings, when the feeling isn't. It carries a person until the love shows. The second is raganuga, practice that follows raga, longing, the spontaneous love of the people of Vraja, Krishna's cowherd village. Its best case: those villagers never checked a rulebook. They followed their hearts toward him, and a practitioner follows their longing. One starts from instruction, the other from attraction. Rupa keeps both. And under every rule he sets a verse he quotes from the Padma Purana. In paraphrase: always remember Vishnu; never forget him. Every rule and every prohibition serves these two. So the schedule on the fridge and the runner's wanting answer to the same thing.
screen: `SADHANA: IT UNCOVERS, NOT BUILDS.` · `VAIDHI: PRACTICE BY RULE.` · `RAGANUGA: PRACTICE BY LONGING.` · then, large: `REMEMBER, AND NEVER FORGET.`

segments.voice: Say out loud, softly, one name you never want to forget: a person, a place, or, if you pray, Krishna or Vishnu. Then breathe, and each time your mind wanders off, say the name once more, gently, without scolding yourself for the wandering.
Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu: a book in which practice, by rule or by longing, clears a window onto a love already real.

howItsDone: In Gaudiya Vaishnava practice, devotees keep daily disciplines such as chanting Krishna's names and hearing the Bhagavata, understood as ways of remembering him; teachers speak of both practice by rule and practice that follows the longing of Vraja.

fork.setup: you're on team rule: practice because scripture asks, every day. now give the other side its best case. why follow longing instead?
options: it starts from attraction, following the love of Vraja's people toward Krishna.
it lets you skip practice on the days you're not in the mood.
it's the only kind of practice Rupa actually accepts.
fork.reveal: Raganuga follows the spontaneous longing of the people of Vraja. It isn't a pass to skip, and Rupa honors practice by rule too.

original.note: Sanskrit sadhana, the means or practice; Rupa's sadhana bhakti is devotion done as practice.

chat.says: Diya says if you don't FEEL it, practice doesn't count. nani says just show up at 7. who's right?
options: both have a case. Rupa keeps rule and longing, and both uncover the love.
Diya. practice without feeling is empty, so wait until the longing comes.
nani. rules are the real devotion, and feelings don't matter at all.
chat.meaning: Rupa honors practice by rule and practice by longing. Either way, practice uncovers a love he calls already real.

sadhana bhakti.meaning: devotion done as practice, with the senses

bhava.meaning: the deeper love for Krishna that practice brings into view

vaidhi.meaning: practice by rule, because scripture asks for it

raganuga.meaning: practice that follows the spontaneous longing of Vraja's people

Vraja.meaning: Krishna's cowherd village in the stories

Padma Purana.meaning: a Sanskrit scripture Rupa quotes on remembering Vishnu

notes: Rupa Goswami block, day 5 of 7 (1665–1671): sadhana bhakti. Strictly this is the second wave of the eastern division, past the very opening; the outline title says 'opening', read here as the opening division. Confirm.
